newsitem.title: UK: Oxford BioMedica details new developments.
newsitem.headline: Oxford BioMedica details new developments.

text.p: Oxford BioMedica Plc said on Wednesday it has agreed with Isis Innovation Ltd. for the exclusive rights to buy a technology known as the Hypoxia Response Element (HRE).
HRE is a gene switch that is used for the selective destruction of solid tumours. Isis is Oxford University's intellectual property company.

Oxford BioMedica, a British-based biomedical company formed in 1995 to develop and commercialise gene therapy technologies, will use this switch to activate anti-cancer genes delivered using its retroviral gene delivery technology.
It said that the purchase of HRE technology has led it to consider bringing forward its anti-cancer clinical trial programme.

Oxford has appointed a clinical consultant to advise on the technical feasibility and resource implications of this acceleration. It noted that a successful accelerated clinical programme would speed up the payback from research it gets.

The company, which was floated on the Alternative Investment Market in December 1996, also announced that it has appointed Chris Bebbington as head of research and Peter Nolan as director of operations.
It has also filed two new patent applications covering a new anti-HIV gene and a gene delivery system for non dividing cells.
Oxford BioMedica's anti-HIV product Immstat is being assembled and tested under contract at Seoul National University in Korea.
